units.title: Organizing Ideas: Claims, Reasons, Transitions and Conclusions
skills: State a clear opinion or topic
Order reasons logically and group related ideas
Link ideas with transitions such as consequently, specifically and in contrast
Write a conclusion related to the opinion or topic
vocab: claim
the main opinion a writer argues for
reason
a statement that explains why the claim is true
evidence
facts, examples or quotations that support a reason
transition
a word or phrase that shows how ideas connect: consequently, in contrast, specifically
logical order
an order that makes sense, such as time order or most important last
concluding statement
a final sentence that sums up and restates the main point

passage.title: A Longer Lunch Break
passage.intro: Muath is writing an opinion essay for his teacher. Read his draft and answer the questions.
paras: (1) Our school should give students a longer lunch break. (2) Right now, students have only twenty minutes to eat. (3) Many of them rush their food or leave it unfinished. (4) Eating too quickly can cause stomachaches. (5) The cafeteria sells juice and water. (6) A longer break would also give students time to rest before afternoon classes. (7) Rested students pay better attention in class.

sentence 2

passage.intro: Hessa wrote an opinion essay. Read her draft and answer the questions.
paras: (1) Coding is the language computers understand, and I believe every student should learn it. (2) Today, computers are used in almost every job, from medicine to farming. (3) Learning to code teaches students to breaking big problems into small steps. (4) Some people say coding is too difficult for young students. (5) However many apps let children learn coding through simple games. (6) In addition, coding helps students express their creativity by building games and websites. (7) In conclusion, coding is a skill that will prepare students for the future.
